content: 1. Administer 5 mg of levonorgestrel orally as soon as possible within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse. The medication is most effective when taken immediately after unprotected intercourse. There are no age restrictions for purchasing this medication over the counter, as the exclusivity age restriction expired on April 30, 2016. 2. The combination of levonorgestrel and antithrombin alfa may reduce the effectiveness of each drug due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. There is a potential risk of thromboembolic disorders. 3. The combination of levonorgestrel and antithrombin III may also reduce the effectiveness of each drug due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 4. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, as a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for therapeutic loss and adjust the dose as needed. 5. Levonorgestrel and argatroban may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 6. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Belzutifan may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding when used with hormonal contraceptives. Advise women of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 7. Levonorgestrel and bemiparin may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 8. Levonorgestrel and bivalirudin may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 9. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Brigatinib induces CYP3A4 in vitro, which may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Brigatinib may also cause fetal harm. 10. The mechanism of interaction between calaspargase pegol and levonorgestrel is unknown. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Due to the potential for indirect interaction, concomitant use of calaspargase pegol with oral contraceptives is not recommended. Advise women of childbearing potential to use a non-oral contraceptive method. 11. Levonorgestrel and dalteparin may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 12. Levonorgestrel decreases the effects of elagolix due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce the efficacy of elagolix. The effects of progestin-only contraceptives on elagolix efficacy are unknown. Advise women to use nonhormonal contraception during treatment with elagolix and for 1 week after discontinuation. 13. Levonorgestrel and enoxaparin may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 14. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control methods. 15. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 16. Levonorgestrel and fondaparinux may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 17. Levonorgestrel and heparin may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 18. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 19. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Lesinurad decreases the effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Use additional nonhormonal contraception methods, as hormonal contraception alone is not reliable when taking lesinurad. 21. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mavacamten may reduce systemic exposure to ethinyl estradiol and progestin, leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for 4 months after the last dose. 23. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Omaveloxolone may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives due to weak CYP3A4 induction. 26. Perampanel decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Levonorgestrel levels are reduced by 40% when coadministered with high-dose perampanel (12 mg/day). Consider backup contraception. 27. Pexidartinib increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity; avoid coadministration with other hepatotoxic agents. 28. Levonorgestrel and phenindione may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 29. Levonorgestrel and pretomanid may increase each other's toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during treatment. 30. Levonorgestrel and protamine may reduce each other's effects due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. There is a risk of thromboembolic disorders. 31. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Repotrectinib is a CYP3A4 inducer, which may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Advise women to use effective nonhormonal contraception. 32. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Sugammadex decreases the effects of levonorgestrel by receptor binding competition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Sugammadex may bind to progestogen, reducing its exposure. If hormonal contraceptives are taken on the same day as sugammadex, use additional nonhormonal contraception for the next 7 days. 34. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, use additional effective nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 35. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates according to product labeling. 36. Levonorgestrel decreases the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance. 37. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of levonorgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 39. Bosentan decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Carbamazepine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Advise women to use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control methods. 42. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clobazam may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 44. Crofelemer increases the levels of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Crofelemer may inhibit CYP3A4 in the gut but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. 45. Levonorgestrel and cyclosporine may increase each other's levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Combined oral contraceptives containing ethinyl estradiol may inhibit cyclosporine metabolism, increasing plasma concentrations. 46. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 47. Dexamethasone decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Efavirenz decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elafibranor may reduce systemic exposure to hormonal contraceptives. Switch to effective nonhormonal contraception or add a barrier method during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. 50. Elagolix decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered and consider increasing their dose if needed. 51. Encorafenib affects levonorgestrel levels by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. 52. Enzalutamide decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Etravirine decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Levonorgestrel and exenatide injectable solution may interact, as exenatide slows gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide. 55. Levonorgestrel and exenatide injectable suspension may interact similarly, as exenatide slows gastric emptying. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide. 56. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 57. Felbamate decreases the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
